prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: production 2D side-view game sprite atlas, genuinely transparent background.
Input image 1 is the established game machinery MATERIAL AND PIXEL STYLE reference. Input image 2 is the existing exterior defense MATERIAL reference. Generate a NEW atlas matching their fine industrial pixel-art texture and subdued dark olive-grey steel, rust confined to seams, restrained warm brass fasteners, occlusion at mechanical joins, upper-left edge light. This is actual sprite artwork, not a mockup.
EXACT layout: FOUR columns, TWO rows, eight equal generously separated cells. Keep each complete object well INSIDE its own cell with at least 35px fully transparent margins. No labels/text, cell lines, shadows outside the objects, environment or floor.
TOP ROW:
1. A small LOW autonomous sentry BASE ONLY, no gun attached. Squat wide anchored steel foot, short compact geared swivel bearing centered on top, protected motor and bolted maintenance hatch. The complete base is wider than tall, width:height about 1.5:1. Clearly compact field equipment, never a tall tower or pedestal. Four readable attachment bolts, short grounded feet.
2. A distinct matching LOW sentry BASE ONLY variant, same size and top bearing position, protected ammo-feed/service housing on its side and a short cable. Wide low body and squat foot. Keep structural mass and proportions consistent with component 1.
3. A compact autonomous MACHINE-GUN HEAD ONLY, pointing precisely RIGHT in orthographic side elevation. Single short perforated barrel, closed recoil receiver, compact optic on top, round pivot near the LEFT third underneath. No pistol grip, no tripod, no pedestal, no person, no twin cannon. Its long slender barrel aims horizontally. Entire component fits strictly inside its own cell.
4. A small field AMMUNITION SERVICE CASE with a folded dark steel handle, worn metal locking clips and small brass feed coupling. Grounded, squat, side elevation. No text or symbols. Same material family, useful alongside the compact sentries.
BOTTOM ROW:
5. A weathered INDUSTRIAL WATER PIPE: tall vertical pipe at LEFT with valve wheel halfway up, bent horizontal elbow across the top ending in short downward-facing open spout on RIGHT. Flat metal foot under left pipe, rusty collars, dark wet mouth and clear material thickness. Approx width:height 1:1. No rendered falling water (animated in game).
6. A single tall narrow electrical CABLE POST: slim textured steel mast with grounded bolted foot, two porcelain insulators at its top, short cross-arm near the top and a tiny closed service junction box halfway down. Height about five times width. No cables attached and no warning letters; hanging cables are animated separately in game.
7. A tall narrow WINDSOCK MAST ONLY: worn metal post with grounded foot, a short horizontal bearing arm at its top pointing right and an attachment ring. No cloth attached. Height about five times width. Material match with component 6 but different silhouette.
8. A WINDSOCK CLOTH ONLY: faded orange and dirty cream fabric bands, wide open attachment ring at the far LEFT, tapering to a thin open end at the RIGHT, extended horizontally; subtle stitched seams and angular pixel fabric shading. Do not draw mast or rope. Cloth is separately deformed by game code.
Camera invariants: true level side-scroller orthographic elevation; vertical posts remain vertical, ground baseline horizontal. Very shallow local edge thickness like reference machinery, no isometric view or receding ground. Do not copy the large old towers. All parts legible when reduced to around 35–70 game pixels. Crisp silhouettes, fine pixel-art texturing, no smooth painterly gradients, plastic or bright mint vector blocks. Transparent negative space and holes; absolutely no black backing rectangle, halo, vignette, baked background, checkerboard or glow. No component may intrude into a neighboring cell.
notes: Original generated alpha preserved. Textures are used as atlas regions with nearest filtering and shared alpha cutoff; animation is driven by game code.
